title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Closing a Denial on the Patient's Decision Not to Request External Review
content:
**Terms of the patient's decision.** On an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) that is a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim in denied status for an Observation Stay Account or an Emergency Department Visit Account where a member-level appeal (a member appeal filed under the patient's authorized-representative form) has been filed, the appeals filed number at least the payer class's available appeal levels, the payer class offers independent external review and the external-review window is still open, the claimant's internal appeals are exhausted and the remaining route is the patient's own request for external review; when the patient decides in person not to request it, the claim's last route ends and this rule takes the services still open off the claim as one write-off entry with the write-off reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED, carrying the claim's current denial reason code, booked through the patient's own decision; any other claim gets nothing here.

**The external-review window.** The external-review window is open while fewer than the payer class's external-review window months have passed since the claim's denial date, counted in whole calendar months: a month is complete on the same day number of a later month, so a date whose day number is below the denial date's has not yet completed that month.

| Hypothetical denial date the 15th of month 1, window 4 months | Whole months passed | Window |
|---|---|---|
| the 14th of month 5 | 3 | open |
| the 15th of month 5 | 4 | closed |

**Recording the decision.** The patient's external-review decision is not recorded until, on an account that carries self-administered drugs and no non-covered patient liability, those drugs carry their non-covered write-off entry on the claim.

**What the write-off amount replaces.** For the services still open on a claim closed under this rule, and only for them, the claim's last route has ended and the amount written off as appeals exhausted is the close-out value rather than the denied amount; small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list, take-home convenience items, the services closed on the member's decision, small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list and self-administered drugs are written off under their own rules, and every other denied amount is written off in full by the hospital, never billed to the patient, when its route ends in a write-off: timely filing expired (no timely-filing proof), no authorization obtained (no authorization, notification, emergency exemption or retro authorization), non-covered with no waiver (no advance waiver on file), appeals exhausted (the last available level upheld the denial), or below the appeal threshold (a denied amount at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount that is not worth appealing).

**What stays on the claim.** The recovered amount above the close-out value and the other write-offs stays on the claim as the agreement's contractual remainder, which Riverbend's month-end contractual close posts on the last calendar day of the month.

Observation Stay Account and Emergency Department Visit Account are patient classes of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) the claim bills.

## The patient's own tool: `close_denial_on_external_review_decision_5747d436`
**Capability.** Records, as the patient, the patient's own decision not to request an independent external review of a denied insurance claim, so that Riverbend closes the denial without billing the patient: one write-off entry with the write-off reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED and the claim's current denial reason code, dated today, for the figure the representative gave, lowering the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. The patient is never billed for it; the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** A customer-owned tool: the agent unlocks `close_denial_on_external_review_decision_5747d436` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters**
- `claim_id` — the reference number of the patient's insurance claim that the representative read to them from the claim lookup.
- `amount_usd` — the figure the representative told the patient Riverbend is closing on their decision: USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent; posted exactly as given.

**Return.** A text receipt: "Decision recorded. Write-off <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED, denial code <carc_code>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The denial code is the claim's denial reason code copied onto the entry; the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer (USD, 2 decimal places). The receipt appearing is the success signal.
